title: Nat Cole standing to sing with the piano as a prop
summary: Willard asks who played piano after Nat stood up to sing; Lee says nobody did, Nat tinkered on stage and Buddy Cole played on records.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: We were back up to now where we left off on Reel 4 where you were with Nat, and you'd talked about
touring the United States, you talked about your first conducting at Cyros, you talked about touring South America ...
And I told you about the bands over there, right?
Uh huh. You mentioned that when Nat eventually became a stand up singer, who played piano when Nat quit playing and just sang?
Was there a piano player? I can't remember. But I saw him then.

No, there wasn't a piano player, but he would always get back to the piano and tinker. The piano was his prop. The piano always sat on stage with him, and a lot of the arrangements had about 8 bars -- orchestra, you know, solo, and he would be tinkering on the piano, then.

But he always kept about 3 things with the trio in the show. He always did. And later on, he had a couple of arrangements made for the trio. He would do 'Tea for Two' -- that was one of them, and he would do 'Route 66' was one he had an arrangement for. But ...
But even with a large orchestra, there was never anybody else playing piano?
